questions.q: What does `dbt_utils.generate_surrogate_key()` do that a hand-written `HASH()` call in Snowflake doesn't?
options: It compiles to whatever hashing function the target warehouse supports and handles nulls consistently, so the same model works unchanged across warehouses
It only works inside Snowflake and nowhere else
It generates a random key with no relation to the input columns
It replaces the need for a unique_key on incremental models
questions.explain: generate_surrogate_key() is warehouse-portable and handles null columns consistently — a hand-rolled HASH() call is Snowflake-specific and can mishandle nulls.

options: Generating a full range of date rows (e.g. one per day) with no source table needed, including days with zero activity
Loading a CSV of dates via dbt seed
Testing that a date column is never null
Converting timestamps between time zones
questions.explain: date_spine() generates a calendar of rows directly — useful because you can't GROUP BY your way to a row for a day that has no underlying data.

options: Selects all columns from a relation except the ones you explicitly list
Selects only columns whose name starts with a given prefix
Runs every model in the project marked with a star config
Generates a surrogate key for every column automatically
questions.explain: star() is useful for 'everything except these specific columns' — common in staging models that exclude a couple of renamed or dropped columns.

options: When combining several tables with overlapping but not identical columns, filling missing columns with null instead of erroring
When you need to delete duplicate rows from a single table
When testing that two columns always match across tables
When installing a package for the first time
questions.explain: union_relations() is designed for the common case of one table per region/year with slightly different column sets, filling gaps with null rather than failing.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why is `dbt_utils` specifically the near-universal package install, versus a smaller specialized package?
options: Its macros solve problems that show up in nearly every warehouse project, already tested across warehouses and maintained by dbt Labs
It is the only package dbt Cloud allows you to install
It is required for dbt seed to function at all
Smaller packages are always buggier by definition
questions.explain: The macros covered (surrogate keys, date spines, unions, pivots) are broadly applicable patterns nearly every project needs, which is why dbt_utils specifically sees near-universal adoption.
